title: Start with your knowledge. Build a better bot.
excerpt: A practical checklist for turning your documents and FAQs into a useful business assistant.
author: TalkToBot editorial
seo_title: Build a bot from your business knowledge
seo_description: Prepare your knowledge, configure your assistant, and test answers before deployment.
body:
# Start with a clear job
Decide what your assistant should help people do. A useful first scope is answering product questions, explaining a service, or helping customers find the right next step.

## Prepare reliable sources
Use current documents and FAQs with clear ownership. Remove obsolete policies and conflicting answers before uploading. A bot is easier to review when every important answer has a recognizable source.

## Test before you deploy
Ask real questions your customers use. Include questions the assistant should not answer. Review citations, unclear responses, and the route to a human colleague.

## Keep improving
Review conversations regularly. Update your sources when your business changes, and re-test important journeys after each significant update.

title: Make lead capture feel like a conversation.
excerpt: Ask for the information you need, at the moment it helps the customer move forward.
author: TalkToBot editorial
body:
# Help first, ask second
A useful conversation starts with the visitor’s question. Explain the next step before requesting contact details.

## Collect only what you need
A name, work email, and a short description may be enough to route an enquiry. Avoid requesting private information that your sales or support team does not need.

## Confirm the details
Show customers what will be submitted and how their team will respond. A model’s guess about someone’s contact information is not a confirmed lead.

## Review the handoff
Check both the conversation and CRM delivery status. A recorded enquiry is different from a verified update in an external system.

title: Your before-launch AI assistant checklist.
excerpt: Knowledge, boundaries, channels, and human handoffs: the checks worth doing before your first customer chat.
author: TalkToBot editorial
body:
# A considered launch
Start with a small set of real customer tasks. Verify those tasks end to end before expanding the assistant’s responsibilities.

## Check the knowledge
Confirm that key policies and answers are current. Ask questions with missing evidence and check that the assistant communicates uncertainty.

## Check the channel
Test the actual website or messaging integration, including permissions, incoming messages, and outgoing delivery failures.

## Check the human handoff
Make it clear when and how a person can help. Confirm your team can find the conversation and act on it.

## Review after launch
Keep a regular review of unanswered questions and customer feedback. Treat your bot’s knowledge as an evolving business resource.
